hero.bio: Six of my nine years in software went into healthcare and home care: I worked in the team behind a booking platform serving 80,000+ users, and on offline-first apps for nurses working in low-coverage areas. Today I ship production products with AI agents — fast, verified, and secure by design.

items.title: Opaline Santé — home-care booking
items.problem: Let patients book home care from independent healthcare professionals — nurses, physiotherapists and others.
items.built: Fullstack developer in the team building Opaline Santé, CBA's booking platform. I also contributed to the shared UI component library, together with the design team.

items.title: Offline-first apps for home care
items.problem: Home-care nursing services (SSIAD, SAD), nursing homes (EHPAD) and meal-delivery teams often work where the mobile network is weak or missing.
items.built: Offline-first Android apps: an embedded SQLite database on the device, synced with the server in the background. Java and Kotlin, later Flutter.
items.result: Care teams keep working without a connection; their data syncs once the network is back.

items.title: Subscription platform for a speech therapist

items.built: The whole platform — Next.js, Supabase (Postgres), Stripe subscriptions, hosted on Vercel — in under 24 hours of total work, directing AI coding agents.

how.title: How I work with AI agents
how.intro: I direct AI coding agents to ship production software fast, and I stay accountable for what ships: architecture, verification, security and maintenance. Speed always comes paired with control.
how.setup: My workflow builds on Lauren Tan's open-source collection of engineering playbooks for AI coding agents, [pstack](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack). I run an adapted subset of it in Claude Code, together with rules that every session loads.

steps.name: Understand
steps.text: Before touching code, the agent explains how the subsystem works and why it was built that way, from the code and its history.

steps.name: Design
steps.text: Types, signatures and module boundaries come before implementation, so the shape gets reviewed while it is still cheap to change.

steps.name: Build
steps.text: The requested scope and nothing more, with unit tests for normal cases, edge cases and errors. No unrequested features, no dead code.

steps.name: Verify
steps.text: Proof is the feature running and the real value, not “it compiles”. A bug is reproduced and traced to its root cause before it is fixed; a performance gain is measured before and after.

steps.name: Review
steps.text: Before shipping: what else the change could break beyond its diff, checked by running code. The final call on what ships is mine.

rules: Every command, flag, package and version is checked against the official documentation, with its source.
Verified facts, assumptions and uncertainties are stated separately.
Infrastructure commands get a dry run first, and a rollback plan is written before the change.
Anything destructive or touching production waits for my explicit confirmation.
how.proof: In practice: [a subscription platform built in under 24 hours](#speech-therapy-platform), and [a WordPress site rebuilt in Next.js in under 45 minutes](#other-work).
